subject: Payload coalesce-induced latency affecting hosted inference — customer advisory & remediation
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@slicewave.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@slicewave.com
Date: 2027-06-18T15:22:00Z
Subject: Elevated per-request latency + truncated tokens since 06/18

Hi Jordan,

We're seeing a noticeable latency increase across our /v1/generate calls starting ~06:10 UTC today and a handful of responses that appear truncated mid-sentence. P95 has gone from ~200ms to ~1.8s for our steady stream and spike to 2.6s during bursts.

Attachment: slicewave_latency_capture_0618.zip (contains packet captures and sample request IDs)

Can you confirm if there are any ongoing disturbances on your side? Our traffic pattern is largely identical to yesterday (short prompts, frequent concatenated context).

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Platform Eng — SliceWave
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@slicewave.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-18T15:41:00Z
Subject: Re: Elevated per-request latency + truncated tokens since 06/18

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the capture. We are investigating with priority. Initial triage shows a correlated rise in small-batch coalescing activity in US-WEST region around 06:08–06:16 UTC.

I've looped in Marissa and Ben from Customer Ops and Infra respectively. We'll keep you posted within the hour with an initial impact statement and temporary mitigations.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@slicewave.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-18T16:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Elevated per-request latency + truncated tokens since 06/18 — initial incident advisory

Hi Alex (and team),

Summary (initial):
- Impact: Elevated end-to-end latency for hosted generation endpoints for a subset of customers routed through US-WEST; some responses saw token truncation due to partial assembly timeouts.
- Start: ~2027-06-18T06:08:00 UTC
- Mitigation in progress: temporarily disabled an aggressive payload-coalescing heuristic on affected routing pools; this has reduced P95 to ~350–450ms for most traffic but a small residual P95 elevation remains for very small payloads (~300–600 tokens).

What we found so far (root-cause hypothesis):
- A new coalescing heuristic deployed in the serving runtime on 06/17 aimed to improve throughput for high-concurrency customers. Under workload characteristics with high variation in prefix length (many short prompts interleaved with longer contexts) the heuristic incorrectly grouped heterogeneous requests into the same GPU batch leading to repeated KV-cache rebinds and extra memory transfers. That path increased end-to-end assembly time and in a few cases hit our safety timeout for streaming chunks, producing truncated responses.

Immediate actions taken:
- Rolled back the heuristic in US-WEST routing pools at 16:00 UTC (06/18) — this is the temporary mitigation.
- Applied a conservative coalescing override for customers with small average prompt lengths (includes SliceWave) to avoid heterogeneous batching for 24 hours.

Next steps / follow-ups:
1) Postmortem and permanent fix: engineering will harden the coalescing logic to respect prefix-length buckets and avoid KV rebinding thrash (JIRA-INC-9452 assigned). ETA: 72 hours for a tested patch, 10 days for staged rollout.
2) Customer communication: we will publish an incident post on status.redwood.ai with timeline and mitigation (link will be provided).
3) Compensation/escalations: If SliceWave observed customer-facing impact (lost revenue or SLA misses), Jordan will coordinate commercial follow-up with Ben.

We apologize for the interruption. Please reply here with any customer-side observations that look unresolved.

Attachments: payload-coalesce-incident-slides.pdf (short slides for customer ops)

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@slicewave.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, ops@slicewave.com
Date: 2027-06-18T16:32:00Z
Subject: Re: Elevated per-request latency + truncated tokens since 06/18 — initial incident advisory

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the temporary override — we can confirm the P95 reduced to ~420ms after 16:05 UTC. A few edge requests still show truncation though (~4 requests per 10k). We'll hold off on rolling back our client-side retries for now.

Can you share the postmortem link once available? We'll want to send a short internal note to our SREs.

Appreciate the detail.
Alex
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@slicewave.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-19T21:05:00Z
Subject: Final incident update and postmortem link

Hi all — follow-up from infra:

What we did (permanent):
- Deployed a fix to the coalescing decision tree that explicitly buckets by prefix-length and model sequence-length distribution, eliminating KV rebinding on heterogeneous batches.
- Added a safety guard to increase the streaming chunk assembly timeout by 150ms for impacted pools while the rollout completes.

Status: Patch rolled to 100% of US-WEST at 20:50 UTC on 2027-06-19. We validated with synthetic load matching SliceWave's profile and saw P95 return to baseline (~210ms). Truncation events reduced to 0.02 per 10k.

Public links:
- Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20270618-27
- Postmortem doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A2b3CoalescePostmortem
- JIRA: JIRA-INC-9452

If SliceWave needs a formal SLA credit request, Jordan — flag and I'll coordinate with finance.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
